title: Kim Ji-won transforms GS Caltex offense, secures Yeosu Cup title - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: They no longer looked only to Silva. The proven finisher's power remained, but the attacking routes became more varied. The changes initiated at the fingertip of setter Kim Ji-won brought GS Caltex a harvest as valuable as the championship trophy. GS Caltex rose to the top by winning three straight matches after losing their first group-stage game at the 2026 Yeosu NH Nonghyup Cup tournament. In the final they succeeded in avenging themselves by defeating Korea Expressway Corporation (KEC) in a 3-2 set score. They also set a new record for the most cup tournament titles overall. As welcome as the championship was the change in offense. Until now GS Caltex had relied heavily on Silva's scoring. Although they had the sure finisher Silva, it was hard to avoid concentrated opponent attention. In this tournament Kwon Min-ji and Thanacha actively joined the attack, lessening Silva's burden. At the center of that was Kim Ji-won. Kim Ji-won adjusted attacking directions according to the flow of the game and the opponent's blocking rather than funneling the ball to a specific player. She used the left and right wings as well as central attacks appropriately, unsettling the opponent's defense. The coordination with the middle blockers stood out in particular. By using quick attacks to draw the opponent's blocking attention to the center, she created favorable situations for the flank attackers as well. With diverse attacking options added to Silva's finishing ability, the structure of the offense improved considerably. Teamwork shone on defense as well. The backcourt defenders tenaciously handled the opponent's hard hits and created counterattack opportunities based on stable consolidation. Even amid the captain Yu Seo-yeon's injury absence, the players faithfully performed their roles and minimized loss of strength. The sweat poured during the off-season also paid off. GS Caltex strengthened cohesion and refined attacking patterns through intense training including a training camp in Japan. The chemistry built during preparation led to the cup tournament victory. Coach Lee Young-taek said, "It was not an easy journey after starting with a loss in the first game, but the training成果 that the coaching staff and players prepared together during the off-season appeared directly in the results," and added, "I want to express my gratitude to the entire squad for staying focused and united until the end under difficult conditions." He went on to say, "Building on the confidence gained from this championship, we will prepare steadily so we can give fans the joy of victory in the upcoming V-League regular season." Of course, cup tournament results do not guarantee regular-season success. Since opponent strength and player deployment change, maintaining offensive diversity consistently is the key. Still, GS Caltex confirmed a clear possibility. The sure finisher Silva combined with the attacking strength of Kwon Min-ji and Thanacha, and Kim Ji-won used them evenly to show a new offensive framework. From volleyball that depended on Silva to volleyball that uses Silva more effectively. It is the most welcome change GS Caltex took home along with the championship trophy. title: GS Shop Expands Private Brands as Bedding Line Sells Out - Seoul Economic Daily
content: Heriden Draws 920 Million Won in Orders in Debut Broadcast GS Shop is accelerating its push into private brands, drawing on nearly three decades of sales data and customer spending patterns. The home shopping operator is using product differentiation to sharpen its competitive edge while shoring up profitability. The company's "Heriden 100% Wool Bedding Set," which can be boiled for washing and launched early this month, sold out during its broadcast with about 2,900 sets purchased, industry sources said on the 19th. Orders totaled 920 million won ($640,000), roughly 150% of the company's initial target. Heriden is GS Shop's own bedding brand, developed over about a year of planning and product work, and the broadcast marked its first appearance before consumers. The company moved into in-house development after bedding orders jumped to about 33 billion won last year from 8 billion won a year earlier, more than tripling as the market expanded. GS Shop paid particular attention to rising consumer demand for premium bedding, with wool products accounting for about 40% of total bedding orders. During development, the company surveyed more than 3,000 customers and incorporated their requests on materials, functionality and ease of washing. The Heriden launch broadens GS Shop's private brand portfolio to four. The bedding line joins VU in beauty, Simple Bio in health supplements and Barosseum in household goods. Existing private brands are also growing quickly. Cumulative orders for VU in the first three quarters of this year surged 470% from a year earlier. Simple Bio orders rose 324% over the same period, while the number of customers placing orders increased 163%. The strategy of strengthening private brands and exclusive products is feeding through to earnings. GS Shop posted second-quarter operating profit of 26.7 billion won, up 6.0% from a year earlier. Operating profit has risen for three straight quarters, from the fourth quarter of last year through the second quarter of this year. Industry analysts point to a 46% year-on-year increase in the number of exclusive products, centered on fashion, beauty and living goods, as a key driver of the improvement. Exclusive products are seen as better suited than standard merchandise to differentiation and margin gains. "Home shopping companies are using sales information and customer purchase data accumulated over many years to strengthen product competitiveness," an industry official said. "Efforts to identify products with strong growth potential and to build up private brands are expected to continue." Original reporting by Kim Kyung-taek for Seoul Economic Daily. content: Team Overcomes Korea Expressway, Credits Training and Unity for Seventh Cup Win ■ Silva-centered powerful offense and setter Kim Ji-won’s ball distribution Based on a stable team strength, the offensive line’s performance was outstanding. While opposite spiker Silva served as the team’s main scorer, Kwon Min-ji and Tana Cha shared the firepower, reducing the offensive burden. Additionally, setter Kim Ji-won’s organic ball distribution diversified the offensive options. Kim actively utilized the middle blockers in quick attacks and blocking situations, breaking down the opponent’s blocking line. The middle blockers also excelled in both offense and defense in the center, establishing themselves as a key axis of the team’s tactics. ■ Defensive stability and the players’ balanced dedication In addition to offense, the stability of the rear defense was a driving force behind the victory. The defensive line maintained focus until the end, connecting the opponent’s key attacks with digs, which played a decisive role in creating smooth counterattacks and shifting the momentum. Although this tournament had the absence of captain and key player Yu Seo-yeon due to injury, all players fulfilled their roles in their respective positions, demonstrating the team’s resilience in turning crises into opportunities as a unified "one team." ■ Solid organizational power forged through Japan training camp and off-season training The foundation of this victory lay in the sweat poured during the off-season. GS Caltex enhanced tactical completeness by undergoing intensive off-season training, including a training camp in Japan. Through repeated training, the team’s overall organizational power became more solid, and they demonstrated rapid growth by showcasing high-completion match performance from the first tournament of the season. ■ Coach Lee Young-taek: "A valuable victory created by the players’ dedication" GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek stated, "Although the journey was not easy after starting with a loss in the first game, the training results prepared by the coaching staff and players during the off-season were fully reflected in the outcome." He added, "I would like to express my gratitude to the entire team for maintaining focus and uniting as one despite the difficult circumstances." He continued, "It is meaningful to repay the unwavering support from the fans with the gift of a championship." He emphasized, "Based on the confidence gained from this victory, we will thoroughly prepare step by step to bring the joy of victory to the fans in the upcoming V-League regular season." ■ Continuing momentum toward the 2026-2027 V-League GS Caltex, which quickly reorganized the team after a loss in the first group stage match and completed the championship with three consecutive wins, once again set a new record for the most cup tournament victories in team history (seven times) through this tournament. GS Caltex plans to accelerate preparations for the upcoming 2026-2027 V-League regular season based on the power and organizational strength confirmed in this cup tournament.

title: GS Caltex Wins Cup Tournament After Three-Year Gap - 조선일보
content: Led by MVP Gisele Silva, GS Caltex secures seventh title with 3-2 victory over Korea Expressway Corporation GS Caltex, the women’s division champion of the V-League last season, claimed the cup tournament title for the first time in three years, led by the performances of ace Gisele Silva, 35, Cuba, and Kwon Minji, 25 years old. GS Caltex, led by head coach Lee Young-taek, defeated Korea Expressway Corporation 3-2 (25-23, 26-28, 18-25, 25-22, 15-5) in the women’s division final of the 2026 Yeosu·NH Nonghyup Cup Professional Volleyball Tournament held at the Yeosu Jinnam Gymnasium on the 18th, securing the championship. This marked their seventh title in the women’s professional volleyball cup tournament, the most ever, three years after their last win in 2023. The two teams, who faced each other in last season’s V-League championship match, engaged in another fierce battle. GS Caltex took the first set with Tana Cha’s quick open attack and Gisele Silva’s back attack at 23-23, but they lost the next two sets to Korea Expressway Corporation, finding themselves on the brink of defeat. In the fourth set, GS Caltex scored first to reach 20 points with contributions from Kwon Minji and Gisele Silva at 17-16. They then extended the match to a fifth set with Gisele Silva’s back attack, Oh Se-yeon’s quick attack and blocking, and Silva’s final open attack. In the fifth set, Korea Expressway Corporation made early errors, while GS Caltex secured an early lead with points from Gisele Silva and Kwon Minji again. GS Caltex was led to victory by ace Gisele Silva, who scored 30 points, and Kwon Minji, who recorded the highest attack success rate of 62.86% and 24 points among all players. Silva was selected as the tournament’s MVP. Korea Expressway Corporation’s main attacker Moma Basoko, 33, Cameroon, who played despite knee pain, fought hard with 31 points but had to settle for second place for the second consecutive year.

title: Market Rout Shakes Up Market Cap Rankings of South Korea’s Top 10 Conglomerates… Hyundai Motor Loses Third Place to LG - IT조선
content: The market capitalization rankings of South Korea's top 10 conglomerates have shifted since the KOSPI peaked in June. LG Group overtook Hyundai Motor Group to claim third place, while GS Group surpassed Lotte Group to move into eighth. LG expanded its market value on the back of growing demand for energy storage systems (ESS), while GS benefited from a booming oil refining industry and expectations surrounding new business opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. According to the Korea Exchange on October 16, the combined market capitalization of South Korea's 10 largest conglomerates by total assets stood at 3,378.8 trillion won as of the previous day, based on common shares. This represents a 43.9% decline from 6,022.3 trillion won on June 22, when the KOSPI reached its peak. However, the figure remains 45.8% higher than the 2,317.7 trillion won recorded at the end of last year. By group, Samsung topped the rankings with a market capitalization of 1,597.3 trillion won, followed by SK at 1,124.3 trillion won, LG at 185.3 trillion won, Hyundai Motor at 179.9 trillion won, HD Hyundai at 102.4 trillion won, Hanwha at 100.0 trillion won, POSCO at 51.9 trillion won, GS at 16.4 trillion won, Lotte at 16.0 trillion won and Shinsegae at 5.2 trillion won. In terms of percentage changes since the KOSPI's June peak, GS was the only group to increase its market capitalization, gaining 10.2%. The other nine groups all recorded declines, though the extent varied considerably. SK suffered the steepest drop at 54.3%, followed by Shinsegae (-48.4%), Hyundai Motor (-41.2%), HD Hyundai (-39.5%), Samsung (-39.1%), Hanwha (-28.9%), LG (-15.5%), Lotte (-13.7%) and POSCO (-11.5%). LG Overtakes Hyundai Motor to Become South Korea's Third-Largest Conglomerate by Market Value One of the most notable changes was the reversal of third and fourth place in the rankings, with LG Group moving up from fourth to third. Three LG affiliates—LG Energy Solution, LG H&H and LG Uplus—managed to increase their share prices despite the broader stock market correction, helping limit the group's overall decline in market capitalization. LG Energy Solution was the biggest contributor. Its preliminary third-quarter operating profit reached 756 billion won, far exceeding market expectations of 326.4 billion won. As a result, its market capitalization increased by approximately 4 trillion won during the period. The strong performance was driven by a roughly 50% quarter-on-quarter increase in energy storage system (ESS) shipments as bottlenecks in battery pack production eased. Growing demand for Korean-made ESS batteries also provided support as the United States restructured its battery supply chains to reduce reliance on Chinese products. LG H&H benefited from expectations that its North American sales would surpass those in China for the first time this year, supported by developments such as the launch of its Dr.Groot haircare brand at Sephora stores in the United States. LG Uplus, meanwhile, attracted investor interest through the expansion of its enterprise infrastructure business, centered on its Paju AI data center, the largest of its kind in the Seoul metropolitan area, as well as increased dividend payouts. Hyundai Motor Group, by contrast, slipped to fourth place. The decline in market capitalization across all 12 of its listed affiliates weighed heavily on the group, with automakers and automotive parts companies suffering particularly steep losses. Since the KOSPI's June peak, Hyundai Motor has lost approximately 59 trillion won in market value, Hyundai Mobis about 21 trillion won and Kia roughly 18 trillion won. The declines reflected downward revisions to earnings expectations amid production disruptions caused by labor strikes, a stronger Korean won and rising raw material costs. Fading enthusiasm surrounding robotics was another major factor. Hyundai Motor Group shares had surged in the first half of the year on expectations for "physical AI," driven by its robotics subsidiary Boston Dynamics. However, investor optimism quickly weakened as the group failed to provide sufficiently detailed strategies for its robotics and autonomous driving businesses. "The stock price has continued to decline due to a lack of concrete strategies for robotics, autonomous driving and software-defined vehicles (SDVs), compounded by lower production volumes resulting from strikes and unfavorable exchange-rate movements caused by the stronger won," said Jang Moon-soo, an analyst at Hyundai Motor Securities. Hyundai Motor experienced production disruptions affecting tens of thousands of vehicles during third-quarter labor strikes, contributing to an approximately 11% year-on-year decline in global wholesale sales. Export profitability also deteriorated as the average won-dollar exchange rate fell by around 80 won compared with the second quarter, reflecting a stronger Korean currency. Kia, meanwhile, recorded higher vehicle sales but suffered weaker profitability as lower-margin electric vehicles accounted for a larger share of sales and the company reduced prices for entry-level EV models in Europe. GS Gains on Refining and Construction, While Lotte Struggles with Retail Weakness GS Group, which shares its roots with LG Group, moved up one place from ninth to eighth as its market capitalization increased. Three listed affiliates contributed to the growth, led by holding company GS Corp., whose market value rose 39.6%. GS Engineering & Construction gained 3.9%, while Xi S&D surged 131.0%. A key driver was the record earnings reported by GS Caltex, the group's unlisted oil refining subsidiary, amid a refining boom linked to developments in the Middle East. Supported by GS Caltex's strong performance, GS Corp. posted consolidated operating profit of 1.7 trillion won in the second quarter, exceeding market consensus estimates by 53%. The group's push into AI data centers also helped boost its corporate valuation. In June, GS Corp. established GS AI Infrastructure as a wholly owned subsidiary and announced plans to build a 1.2-gigawatt (GW) AI data center in Donghae, Gangwon Province, by 2028. The company aims to expand the facility's capacity to 2.4 GW over the longer term. "This business could increase net profit by 50% to 200% within three to four years," said Jeon Woo-je, an analyst at KB Securities. "It could serve as a catalyst for the revaluation of GS, which has long traded at a discount." Lotte Group, meanwhile, fell from eighth to ninth place. Since June 22, seven of its 11 listed affiliates have experienced declines in market capitalization. Lotte Shopping lost approximately 2.68 trillion won in market value, Lotte Chemical shed around 740 billion won and Lotte Corp. declined by roughly 290 billion won. Lotte Shopping's valuation weakened as sales growth at its department stores, which had supported first-half earnings, began to slow. The stronger won encouraged more overseas travel, contributing to slower growth in sales to foreign customers. At the same time, the weakening momentum of the KOSPI reduced expectations that a booming stock market would stimulate consumer spending. The sharp decline in Lotte Shopping's market value also cost it the position of Lotte Group's largest listed affiliate by market capitalization, which was taken over by secondary battery materials producer Lotte Energy Materials. Lotte Chemical faced additional pressure after international oil prices plunged in July amid expectations that geopolitical risks in the Middle East would ease. The decline in oil prices dragged down petrochemical product prices. Inventory valuation gains that the company had enjoyed during the first half, when raw material prices surged, subsequently disappeared, increasing the likelihood that Lotte Chemical would return to an operating loss in the third quarter. Lotte Corp., the group's holding company, was also weighed down by falling share prices among its major subsidiaries and the financial burden associated with investments in Lotte Biologics, according to analysts. "As AI data centers have emerged as a major theme in stock markets worldwide, companies involved in related businesses are likely to receive favorable valuations," said Lee Sang-heon, a senior research analyst at iM Securities. "Market expectations surrounding AI data center businesses will continue to influence changes in the market capitalization of individual conglomerates," he added.

title: The Bike That Makes A Strong Case For Owning Just One Motorcycle - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update There probably isn't a rider who has spent enough time on two wheels who hasn't stayed up at night building the perfect multi-bike garage in their head. A Sportster S for Sunday blasts and a CRF300L for when the pavement runs out. A Ninja 1100SX for the fast stuff and an NC750X for the sensible stuff. The permutations are practically endless, and for a while, having the right bike for every job sounds like the ideal setup. Then reality gets involved. Ride one bike more than the others and the neglected machines start looking rather pointless, while every additional motorcycle brings another round of upkeep. Fortunately, modern motorcycles have gotten remarkably good at doing several jobs at once. The trick is finding one that can cover enough ground that the second bike starts looking unnecessary. Adventure bikes have quietly become the motorcycle world's answer to the awkward question of, “If I could only keep one, which one would it be?” They can tour, commute, carry a passenger, eat up broken roads and, when the pavement finally gives up, keep going without much drama. They aren't particularly interested in being the absolute best at any one of those jobs, and that's kind of the point. Some lean harder toward the dirt, others are clearly happier on asphalt, while different engine sizes and price tags make the category broad enough to cover everything from relatively approachable machines to premium flagships. BMW has been playing this particular game for a very long time. The R 80 G/S showed up in 1980 with a fairly simple idea: take the company's boxer-powered road-going motorcycles and give them enough off-road ability to make the end of the pavement feel more like an invitation than a warning. Even the name gave the game away. G/S stood for Gelände/Straße, essentially off-road/road, and the bike went on to define what we now know as the adventure motorcycle. The formula stuck, and so did the GS name. All these ADVs kept stretching the idea in different directions, with each generation becoming more capable and more sophisticated. Then, in 2024, BMW went back to the drawing board for a complete ground-up redesign. That brings us to the R 1300 GS, now practically synonymous with the quintessential big-bike all-rounder. Calling it a facelift or routine model update would undersell the changes. It's almost a motorcycle version of the Ship of Theseus: the GS name and familiar boxer formula remain, but BMW replaced so much underneath that this is effectively a new machine. The boxer was redesigned, the six-speed gearbox moved underneath it for a more compact powertrain, and the old tubular-steel frame gave way to a new sheet-metal steel frame. The rear subframe became die-cast aluminum, the Telelever and Paralever were reworked, and the extensive redesign shaved 26 pounds from the previous model. Ah, the boxer. Fire one up and those cylinders sticking out either side give the engine its unmistakable character, with that familiar side-to-side rocking motion as the crank spins. BMW has been refining this layout for decades, and in the R 1300 GS it has grown to 1,300cc and produces 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque. BMW also moved the six-speed gearbox underneath the engine, rather than having it mounted behind the boxer as before, helping create a more compact powertrain and centralize mass in the chassis. The cylinders still hang out in the breeze, though, because some things are simply too GS to mess with. The 145-horsepower peak arrives at 7,750 rpm, leaving plenty of additional engine speed above the torque-heavy portion of the rev range for stronger acceleration when the road opens up. At 110 pound-feet, it also out-torques the Ducati Multistrada V4 (92 pound-feet), Honda Africa Twin (77.4 pound-feet), and Harley-Davidson Pan America 1250 (94 pound-feet). If you're buying a motorcycle like this, you're definitely going to do some touring. This is where it's important not to confuse the R 1300 GS with the R 1300 GS Adventure. The regular GS doesn't get the Adventure's huge 7.9-gallon tank or its 593-pound curb weight, instead using a five-gallon tank and weighing 523 pounds ready to ride. What it does get is Dynamic Cruise Control, heated grips, an adjustable windscreen, a 33.4-inch standard seat height and a flat tank-seat line BMW designed around long-distance ergonomics. Add the optional Vario luggage (BMW's expandable hard cases that can change their storage capacity depending on how much gear you're carrying), comfort seat and other touring equipment, and there's plenty here for putting serious miles between fuel stops. The suspension is where BMW's unusual approach gets interesting. Up front, the EVO Telelever uses a wishbone-style linkage and a central shock absorber, separating the handlebar's steering movement from the suspension's compression and extension. At the rear, the EVO Paralever pairs a single-sided swingarm with BMW's shaft-drive system. Both ends offer substantial travel, with 7.5 inches up front and 7.9 inches at the rear, while the optional Dynamic Suspension Adjustment adds electronic suspension adjustment, load compensation and spring-rate adjustment. The R 1300 GS gets the kind of electronic safety net you'd expect from a modern flagship, with traction control and lean-angle-sensitive ABS working with the bike's sensors to account for things like lean angle and wheel speed. Hill Start Control helps when setting off on an incline, while Dynamic Cruise Control takes some of the work out of long highway runs. Keyless Ride lets the rider start the bike without pulling out a key, while tire-pressure monitoring keeps tabs on both tires from the cockpit. There's also a 6.5-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity and a dedicated charging compartment with a USB socket, while buyers can add BMW's optional radar-based Riding Assistant with Active Cruise Control and additional collision-warning functions. Automatic and semi-automatic transmission systems are becoming increasingly common across the motorcycle world, and BMW has its own take on the idea with the optional Automated Shift Assistant, or ASA. It removes the need for the rider to operate the clutch manually, while the gearbox can still be controlled through the conventional foot shifter. Put it in automatic mode and the system handles the gear changes itself, using information such as engine and transmission speed, clutch position and the selected riding mode to determine when to shift. Manual mode is still available when the rider wants to choose the gear without having to operate a clutch lever. The R 1300 GS has rivals from across the globe, like the Multistrada V4 and Africa Twin, but its do-it-all recipe is hard to beat, especially if you're aiming for a one-bike garage. title: GS Caltex Wins Cup Final Rematch Against Korea Expressway Corporation - 조선일보
content: Volleyball team avenges earlier loss, claims seventh title in franchise history Women’s professional volleyball team GS Caltex grows stronger in the finals. The team claimed victory once again in a “return match” against Korea Expressway Corporation, whom they faced in last season’s championship finals, to ascend to the summit of the cup tournament. GS Caltex narrowly defeated Korea Expressway Corporation with a set score of 3-2 (25-23, 26-28, 18-25, 25-22, 15-5) in the women’s division final of the 2026 Yeosu·NH Nonghyup Cup Professional Volleyball Tournament, held on October 18 at the Yeosu Jinnam Gymnasium. This win avenged their earlier group-stage loss to Korea Expressway Corporation in the same tournament and solidified their prospects of a two-peat in the new season, having already secured the cup title. The final match drew attention as a rematch of last season’s championship series. At the time, GS Caltex, which ranked third in the regular league, advanced to the championship finals after the semi-playoffs and playoffs. Their opponent was Korea Expressway Corporation, the regular league champion. The result was a three-game sweep by GS Caltex. Korea Expressway Corporation appeared stronger in this tournament. On October 12, during the group stage in Group B, they defeated GS Caltex 3-1. Korea Expressway Corporation showcased solid offensive and defensive balance, conceding only one set until the semifinals. However, in the final, GS Caltex “awakened.” Their “triangular trio” of Gisele Silva, Kwon Min-ji, and Tanacha Suksot shone brightly. The three players combined for a staggering 73 points, demonstrating overwhelming firepower. Silva alone scored 30 points. Silva, who performed exceptionally in every match of the tournament, was also named the Most Valuable Player (MVP). In the first set, GS Caltex’s resilience was on full display. Despite trailing 5-11 early on, they rallied to tie at 13-13, fueled by revived defensive efforts. Silva and Suksot then ignited their scoring spree. After a fierce battle, they staged a comeback to win 25-23, seizing the initiative. Korea Expressway Corporation fought back. In the second set, their “ace” Letitia Moma Basoko led the attacks, while Park Jeong-ah and Kim Se-in combined for 8 points. After a series of deuces, Korea Expressway Corporation claimed the second set. In the third set, GS Caltex unraveled with 8 unforced errors, losing the set by a 7-point margin. From this point, GS Caltex’s focus intensified. In the fourth set, Silva and Kwon Min-ji scored 9 and 6 points, respectively. The match proceeded to the decisive fifth set. GS Caltex gained momentum, while Korea Expressway Corporation struggled with unforced errors. GS Caltex surged ahead early, leading 8-3. Silva and Kwon Min-ji, sensing victory, tightened their offensive grip. They clinched the set 15-5, a 10-point margin, securing the championship. This marked their seventh cup tournament title in franchise history. Basoko recorded 31 points, but the lack of support from domestic players left a bitter taste. Korea Expressway Corporation’s “homegrown ace” Kang So-hwi managed only 6 points.

title: GS Caltex Ends Three-Year Cup Drought With 3-2 Victory - 조선일보
content: Silva, Kwoun Min-ji, and Tanacha Lead GS Caltex to Seventh Cup Title in Team History [OSEN=Cho Eun-hye Reporter] GS Caltex defeated Korea Expressway Corporation to claim victory in the cup tournament. Led by head coach Lee Young-taek, GS Caltex triumphed 3-2 (25-23, 26-28, 18-25, 25-22, 15-5) against Korea Expressway Corporation in the final of the 2026 Yeosu·NH Nonghyup Cup Professional Volleyball Tournament held at the Yeosu Jinnam Gymnasium on the 18th. This marked their first cup tournament victory in three years and the seventh in the team’s history. GS Caltex took the first set. Korea Expressway Corporation initially led 8-3 with attacks from Moma and Kang So-hwi, blocks and quick attacks from Kim Se-bin. However, GS Caltex overturned the deficit at 15-15 with a quick attack by Choi Ga-eun. The set remained tightly contested, and GS Caltex secured the first set with a quick open attack by Tanacha and a back attack by Silva at 23-23. The second set ended in a fierce deuce battle, with Korea Expressway Corporation staging a comeback. Trailing 15-17, Korea Expressway Corporation took the lead with a back attack by Moma and an open score by Park Jung-ah. GS Caltex responded immediately, and the teams continued to exchange points. GS Caltex first claimed a set point with a score by Tanacha, but Korea Expressway Corporation countered with a quick open attack by Mami. Ultimately, Korea Expressway Corporation secured the second set 28-26 after Moma’s open score at 26-26 and a net violation by Kim Ji-won of GS Caltex. Korea Expressway Corporation carried their momentum into the third set. Leading 11-5 with service points by Kim Se-bin, attack points by Mami, quick attacks by Kim Hyun-ji, and opponent errors, Korea Expressway Corporation comfortably built their lead. They further extended their advantage, holding GS Caltex to 14 points and reaching 20 points to claim the set. However, GS Caltex took the fourth set, bringing the match back to square one. Leading 17-16, GS Caltex reached 20 points with Kwoun Min-ji and Silva leading the charge. They added points with Silva’s back attack, Oh Se-yeon’s quick attack and block, and clinched the set with Silva’s open score to force a fifth set. In the decisive fifth set, GS Caltex completely dominated Korea Expressway Corporation. Korea Expressway Corporation committed frequent errors, while GS Caltex surged ahead with Silva and Kwoun Min-ji. At 5-2, Kwoun Min-ji blocked Moma’s attack to extend the lead to 6-2. The gap widened to 10-3, and GS Caltex closed out the match. Silva scored 30 points, Kwoun Min-ji 24, and Tanacha 19 to lead the team to victory. Notably, Kwoun Min-ji achieved a 62.86% attack success rate. Korea Expressway Corporation’s Moma fought hard with 31 points but could not prevent the loss. Kim Se-bin scored 11 points, while Mami and Kim Se-in each contributed 10 points.

title: JPM, GS, MS Stocks Edge Higher After-Hours — Banks Lift Dividends And Announce Buybacks After Fed Stress Test - Stocktwits
content: Shares of JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM), Morgan Stanley (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) edged higher in after-hours trading on Wednesday after the banks announced higher dividends and buybacks following the Federal Reserve’s stress test, which showed the banking sector remains well positioned to withstand a severe economic downturn. At the time of writing, JPM stock was up 0.6% after-hours after closing the regular session down 0.21%, while MS shares gained 0.4% and GS stock was up 0.1%. JPMorgan Chase & Co announced a $50-billion share repurchase program and raised its quarterly dividend as part of updated shareholder return plans. The bank said its board also intends to increase its quarterly dividend 10% to $1.65 per share, up from $1.50 per share, for the third quarter of 2026. The new buyback program will take effect from July 1, alongside the updated shareholder return plans. Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO of JPMorgan Chase, said, “The Board’s intended dividend increase is supported by our consistent investment in our business and strong financial performance. The new share repurchase program provides us with the flexibility to deploy capital in ways that enhance shareholder value over time.” Goldman Sachs (GS) also increased its quarterly dividend by 11% to $5 per share from $4.50, pointing to strong earnings momentum and a robust capital position. The revised payout implies an annual dividend of $20 and will take effect on July 1, pending board approval. Morgan Stanley (MS) similarly announced a 15% hike in its quarterly dividend to $1.15 per share from $1. In addition, the firm said its board has reauthorized a multi-year share repurchase program of up to $20 billion, with no fixed end date, set to begin in the third quarter. The announcement by JPMorgan Chase & Co comes after the U.S. Federal Reserve released the results of its annual stress test. It showed that large banks are well positioned to withstand a severe recession and continue lending to households and businesses. The Fed said that despite more than $708 billion in total loan losses under the hypothetical scenario, aggregate capital declined only 1.6 percentage points and remained above minimum requirements. It added that all 32 banks tested stayed above their minimum common equity tier 1 capital requirements under a scenario that included a severe global recession, a 39% drop in commercial real estate prices, a 30% fall in house prices and an unemployment rate peaking at 10%. title: Will Oil Prices Decline as Middle East Supply Recovers? - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Oil prices are expected to moderate over the next year as supply from the Middle East gradually recovers, according to Goldman Sachs Research. However, high prices may last longer than anticipated given the risk of renewed escalation in the conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran. A barrel of benchmark Brent crude oil is expected to trade at $90 in December 2026, a slight increase from a recent forecast of $85, according to Daan Struyven, co-head of global commodities research and head of oil research. Struyven predicts the Brent price will average $80 a barrel in 2027. “We maintain our base case that continued adaptation of Middle East supply will eventually reduce crude oil prices, while potential renewed escalation still poses significant net upside risk,” Struyven and his team write in a report. The supply of oil from the Middle East declined after the outbreak of the conflict, but exporters have adapted faster than expected. Our researchers estimate that Persian Gulf oil exports have rebounded and have been around their 2025 average since late September. That calculation includes an estimated four million barrels per day (mb/d) of “dark” exports—shipments on tankers that keep their transponders turned off to hide their movements. Given the recovery in exports from the Middle East, why is the price of oil still so high? A barrel of dated Brent crude scheduled for delivery in the next month is trading at more than $130, while benchmark Brent futures have recently been above $100. “Physical prices remain elevated because escalation threatens supply while near-record-low global inventories fuel strong restocking demand,” Struyven writes. For example, Iran or the Houthis could target oil infrastructure in the region, including ports, pipelines, and oil fields. Struyven estimates that spot prices for Brent crude include a nearly $25 risk premium on top of their fair value because supply could be curtailed and inventories could be drawn down further if there is an escalation. At the same time, the sensitivity of global stocks and bonds to oil prices has created increasing demand for oil as a hedge for portfolios. This is another factor helping keep prices high. Helping to keep prices in check, on the other hand, is the base case expectation that the balance between supply and demand in the global market for crude oil and other liquid fuels will shift to a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026 and in 2027, the researchers find. Struyven describes this as “the key driver” of his team’s forecast for crude prices to moderate. In fact, the oil market was nearly balanced in September. Goldman Sachs Research estimates that demand exceeded supply by just 0.3 mb/d that month, a dramatic easing from the 7.2 mb/d supply deficit in March. The market’s return to balance is likely the result of higher non-Gulf oil production and a decline in global oil demand, offsetting the remaining deficit in production from the Persian Gulf. Also, the crude oil market was operating with a surplus in 2025. Global demand for oil declined by roughly 1.3 mb/d in September 2026 compared with the 2025 average as oil prices climbed, Struyven writes. The recovery of Persian Gulf oil shipments, as producers adapt to the conflict there, also supports the base case that the oil market will soon be back in balance, Struyven writes. His team expects the supply of oil from the Persian Gulf to “trend higher as continued adaptation and added transportation resources—especially pipelines and a larger tanker fleet—support further gains,” he adds. Finally, our commodities analysts say that the shock to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz is likely to continue to weigh on the global demand for oil, bringing the market nearer to balance. Oil demand in the third quarter of 2026 was down by 3.3 mb/d year-over-year, “with much of the weakness concentrated in China, the Middle East, and OECD Asia,” Struyven writes. Our analysts estimate that global oil demand in the third quarter was nearly 4 mb/d below its hypothetical path if there had been no oil shock from the war in Iran. They assume that 80% of this gap between actual global demand and the counterfactual will unwind by the fourth quarter of 2027, with the dropoff in demand narrowing to 0.7 mb/d as the availability and affordability of refined oil products gradually improve. “This forecast that oil demand largely recovers is directionally consistent with the demand recovery from prior negative oil supply shocks in 2011 and 2022, and our view that the weakness in Chinese petrochemicals oil demand is largely unsustainable,” Struyven writes. Still, the expected 0.7 mb/d hit to global oil demand that is forecast for the fourth quarter of 2027 reflects the team’s finding that the oil shock has accelerated behavioral changes, especially in the use of existing electric vehicles and trucks in China instead of oil-based equivalents and in electric vehicle sales. title: Birdie G’s Resurrects With a ‘70s-Drenched Dining Room and the Beloved Pickle Chick - Eater Los Angeles
content: The Midwest and Jewish–inflected restaurant will open at Fairmont Century Plaza on October 26 Jeremy Fox’s beloved Santa Monica restaurant, Birdie G’s, will resurrect at Fairmont Century Plaza after closing at the end of 2025. Named after Fox’s daughter Birdie and grandmother Gladys, the restaurant will reopen on October 26, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner with a mix of original favorites, such as the Pickle Chick, and new dishes, including a Rancho Gordo bean–based poached egg ribollita. When Fox first spoke with Fairmont Century Plaza about Birdie’s G’s in June 2025, it was supposed to be the restaurant’s second location. But as it became increasingly clear that the Bergamot Station Arts Center outpost could not remain open, nothing was set in stone; at the time of the closure, Fox believed Birdie G’s might be gone for good. “In life, you very rarely get second chances, and in a restaurant even less so,” he says. “So I feel very fortunate and grateful that I didn’t have to tell Birdie that her restaurant was done.” Add Eater as a preferred source to see more of our reporting on Google. While the original Birdie G’s served only dinner, the Century City location will open at 6 a.m. for coffee, with its Midwest and Jewish–inflected breakfast and lunch available from 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and dinner from 5:30 to 9:30 p.m. The breakfast menu opens with Birdie’s muesli crowned with banana and apple, along with a cornbread waffle paired with sweet pepper jam, citrusy blood orange agrumato-dressed avocado toast, a build-your-own omelet, koji-marinated steak and eggs, and a smoked fish platter. Lunch brings a corned beef Reuben on Bub & Grandma’s bread, rice flour–batter mushroom fritto misto, the return of the famed gluten-free pickle chicken, three sizes of steak frites spanning eight to 28 ounces, and cauliflower kugel. The dinner menu, which offers many of the same dishes as lunch, sees the return of the Hangtown Brei with fried oyster and pork belly that Fox describes as “very decadent, over-the-top, semi-blasphemous,” lamb à la sales, and the stained-glass-like rose petal pie, plus new options such as rotisserie chicken and vegetables. “I like to refer to it as bubbe cuisine,” Fox says. “Just trying to channel that kind of no-nonsense, bare-bones, straight-to-the-point cooking.” The restaurant will also bring back some of Birdie G’s former staff, including bar director Stephanie Redding, who will consult on the drinks; Laura Eldrige, who will work in the bar; and former cooks. Over the years, Fox and the Birdie G’s team documented most of their recipes, which will be the basis for the new location. Birdie G’s in Santa Monica is the first restaurant Fox designed from the ground up; looking back, he says he didn’t quite understand the process or know how to advocate for his ideas at the time. “It was a really cool warehouse space, but nothing about it tied into the concept, the vibe, the atmosphere, to what I wanted Birdie G’s to be,” Fox says. In Century City, he collaborated with EDG Design to help bring his initial vision to fruition. The restaurant stands in stark contrast to the rest of the upscale hotel, bathed in neutral stone and punctuated by indoor greenery. Strong 1970s inspiration permeates the dining room, from the burnt-mustard banquettes to the plaid bar stools and repeating triangular wallpaper that looks like it could be found in a retro basement. Artwork shaped into small galleries adorns the walls, including vintage magazine covers like a 1987 Sports Illustrated issue featuring Joe Carter and Corey Snyder of the Cleveland Indians (now Guardians), and a painting of two birds in dinner coats. “It definitely feels like you’re somewhere else in time, somewhere else in the country,” Fox says. For Fox, Birdie G’s was never meant to be a hotspot. Instead, he hoped the restaurant would feel like it had been there forever; it was initially inspired by his love of chain restaurants like Applebee’s and the Cheesecake Factory. Fox points to 1996’s Big Night as something that influenced him to go to culinary school at all. While he worked in fine dining at restaurants including Rustic Canyon, he kept returning to the cozy Italian restaurant run by the brothers in Big Night as a reference for what he hoped to do. “I wanted that restaurant that was simple, that was earnest, that wasn’t trendy,” Fox says. Decades into Fox’s career, the Century City Birdie G’s feels like something entirely new for him. He says that over the last five years, as he and the industry faced numerous difficulties, it’s been hard to operate as a confident creative force. When Birdie G’s closed in Santa Monica, he suddenly faced, for the first time in many years, not having somewhere to report to every day. Now, as he prepares to reopen Birdie G’s and continues developing his San Luis Obispo restaurant, Edna, he’s feeling hopeful about what is next. “This is me really needing a W,” Fox says. “Really needing a win.” Reservations for Birdie G’s are available on OpenTable. Liam Lawson will make his debut in VCARB's Garage Sessions music and culture event ahead of the United States Grand Prix at Austin, while launching his very own custom Taylor Guitars LL30 GS Mini Special Edition. The guitar features a pink to white ombre design, and his racing number 30 in the centre. Liam has loved music since his childhood, as his Dad encouraged him and his brother to play from the age of six. Not quite the career path Liam ended up taking, though. The event kicks off on Thursday at Inn Cahoots on Austin’s East 6th Street, with the Esses Bazaar from 3pm, featuring live music, food, western wear, glam stations, tattoos and a chance to get up close and grab a photo with the team’s show car. Garage Sessions follows at 7pm, where Liam will perform live next to his former childhood bandmates, including his brother and two close friends! The wider line up features a mix of emerging talent and established songwriters like Jonathan Capeci, Scoot Teasley, Jess Farren, Alison Nichols, and Drake Milligan. Liam said: “I feel very proud to be launching my partnership with Taylor Guitars at Garage Sessions. Playing the guitar has been a big part of my life since I was young, as my Dad played in a band throughout my childhood. He encouraged my brother and I to play since we were six years old, so it feels like a full circle moment to be launching a custom LL30 GS Mini SE while performing with my brother and two friends who I grew up playing with. "Music is a big part of my life, and I use it to clear my head during the season, so I'm really excited to perform at Garage Sessions where we can connect with fans outside of the track. I’m look ing forward to meeting everyone there.” With Garage Sessions bringing together racing, music, and community, Racing Bulls is giving fans another reason to get excited about Austin, and giving Lawson a chance to show off a skill that doesn’t involve a steering wheel.
